analysis.investment_thesis: Inox Green is priced at 129x EV/EBITDA for a business earning 1% ROE that destroyed capital for six consecutive years before generating a thin INR 22 Cr profit — the market is pricing in a transformation that seven years of operating history provides no evidence for. At a free cash flow yield below 1% with contracting EBITDA, there is no margin of safety whatsoever.
key_strengths: Balance sheet dramatically cleaned up — borrowings collapsed from INR 1,411 Cr (2021) to INR 95 Cr (2025), D/E now just 0.05x
Captive O&M relationship with parent Inox Wind provides revenue visibility and recurring contract base
Renewable energy tailwind in India — wind capacity additions could organically expand the O&M fleet
key_risks: Valuation is grotesque: 129x EV/EBITDA for a company earning INR 94 Cr EBITDA on INR 236 Cr revenue — any disappointment is catastrophic
Revenue has a negative 7-year CAGR of -6.1% and EBITDA is in a contracting trend; the 2025 net profit of INR 22 Cr is actually lower than 2024's INR 28 Cr
Other income (INR 57 Cr) now exceeds operating income (INR 52 Cr) — core wind O&M operations are barely earning anything at all
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 129x: priced for perfection in a business with a six-year history of losses
Core operations effectively unprofitable: strip out INR 57 Cr other income and operating profit of INR 52 Cr yields a near-zero net result
INR 637 Cr investing outflow in FY25 funded by INR 572 Cr equity raise — massive dilution with no visible returns yet
ROCE of 2.60% is well below any reasonable cost of capital — the business is an active destroyer of economic value at current prices
FII holding a mere 8.97% and DII 1.52% — sophisticated institutional capital is not buying this story at these levels
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The second-level question here is not "is renewable energy a good sector?" — of course the market knows it is. The real question is: what does INR 163/share (INR 6,549 Cr market cap) already price in? At 129x EV/EBITDA and 22x revenue, the stock is implying a multi-year hockey-stick ramp in earnings that has absolutely no historical support. Revenue in FY25 (INR 236 Cr) is barely above FY18 (INR 368 Cr was inflated) and is essentially flat with FY22. EBITDA peaked around INR 128 Cr in FY20 and has contracted to INR 94 Cr in FY25. The company only crossed into net profitability in FY24 — and is already declining in FY25. This is not a business inflecting upward; it is a business fighting to hold its ground.

The quality of FY25 earnings is alarming. Operating income was INR 52 Cr, yet other income was INR 57 Cr — meaning the reported net profit of INR 22 Cr is entirely reliant on non-operational items. The large FY25 investing outflow (INR 637 Cr) suggests the company is building power generation assets, funded by equity dilution. If this bet pays off, EBITDA could improve — but minority shareholders are bearing execution risk at a price that assumes the bet has already been won. With a free cash flow yield under 1% and ROCE at 2.6% versus a cost of equity comfortably above 12%, the market is demanding the investor absorb all the risk while offering none of the upside. Howard Marks' iron rule applies here: great story, disastrous price.
